The October edition · Season 2 · No. 4

Five trophies and a sixteen-goal month

October was the month the Sixteen won everything that was not nailed down. Five of the eight college conference titles, twenty-five Youth League matches from twenty-five, and Milan Iloski scoring more goals in thirty-one days than eleven of our clubs managed in the league. And yet the table has Washington on top by a point, Georgia with four games in hand, and the top eleven separated by eight points.

By the Touchline desk · read from the save on Monday, October 31, 2022

What this edition is. Touchline has gone monthly, so this is a bigger issue: the full table and all forty-two league results from October, the power rankings, the first Player of the Month, every one of the 352 players graded and ranked against his own position, the development desk, all five conference finals, the Youth League group stage, a World Cup preview with our starting eleven, the Under-20 championship, the 2023 mock draft, the Class of 2022 in the pros — and the Garrett file, which has a date on it now.

The month in one line. Washington went unbeaten in the league (three wins, two draws), lifted the Pac-12, and sit top on 27. Florida State won all five of their league matches in October, the only club to win five. Oklahoma won four and drew one. Georgia played exactly one league game all month — it finished eleven–nil.

October in the league

Every Academy result from the month

Forty-two league matches, 219 goals. Gold-edged tiles are meetings between two of the Sixteen; the rest are the Sixteen against the six schools outside it, which is where most of the big numbers come from.

15pts Florida State

Five from five

The only perfect October in the league: five wins, twelve scored, four conceded — including 1–0 at the champions. Fifteenth on Sep 30, eighth now, and the form team of the month.

4games in hand Georgia

Unbeaten, unhurried

Georgia played one league match in October and won it 11–0 against Clemson, with four for Richard Ledezma. Eight played, still unbeaten, eighteen points — and four games in hand on Washington.

12–0 Michigan

Biggest win of the month

Folarin Balogun scored five against Louisville, including four inside twenty-one minutes. Michigan also lost 2–1 at USC on October 25, which is the Michigan season in miniature.

3draws Washington

Top, narrowly

Washington have drawn three of their twelve league games — 3–3 with Oklahoma and 1–1 at Alabama in October — and lead the league anyway. They are the only one of the Sixteen with a single league defeat.

2–5 Miami

The home defeat

Miami led Texas Tech at home and lost 2–5, Omar Sowe scoring twice. It was their fifth league defeat, level with USC for the most among the Sixteen outside Florida.

0league wins TCU

Twelve and none

TCU are the last winless club in the Academy: twelve played, a draw at Duke, ninety-four conceded. Miami put nine past them and North Carolina ten.

Points rate, goal difference, the grades and squad ability · movement since Sep 30

The model weighs points per game (35%), goal difference per game (25%), the average Touchline Grade of each club’s best eleven (20%) and the average ability of the same eleven (20%). It is deliberately less impressed by the table than the table is.

Michigan

8–0–3 · 24 pts · +42 · 4th in the table · top-11 ability 116.5 · top-11 grade 78.7

Back to first. Michigan are fourth in the table with three defeats, but no squad in the league combines their ability and their production: the highest-graded eleven in the competition (78.7 on average), the Big Ten title — 5–0 over Notre Dame in the final — and Matko Miljevic still level at the top of the grades on 99. A 2–1 defeat at USC is the only reason this is not unanimous.

Player of the month

October 1–31 · all competitions
LSU · Advanced Forward · 22 years old

Milan Iloski

16Goals
2Assists
9Matches
8.66Avg rating
3Player of match

Sixteen goals in nine matches, in three competitions, in one month. Only two of them came in the league — a penalty against Louisville and a late one in the 8–0 against Oregon. The rest came in the Southeastern Conference and the Youth League, where his fifteen goals this season lead the entire competition, ahead of Milan’s Gabriele Capanni on eight. He is thirty goals into the season in 1,118 minutes, a goal every 37 minutes.

His Touchline Grade has gone from 84.9 at the end of September to 99.0, level with Matko Miljevic at the top of the scale. The part that should worry the rest of the league is who he is: a 22-year-old with a current ability of 106, which is 58th among the Sixteen’s forwards and wingers by the game’s own numbers. Only one player in the league is outplaying his rating by more, and it is LSU’s own sixteen-year-old goalkeeper, Nicholas Taylor.

He graduates next summer, and he is fifteenth on our 2023 board because the board still weighs ceiling heavily. If he does this again in November, that will have to change.

Touchline Grades

Month two · every player scored against his own position

The grade measures what a player did, never what the game says he is: every one of the 352 players is scored against the others doing his exact job, on the numbers that job is for, with average rating capped at a quarter of the weight and small samples pulled toward the middle. Sixty-one is average; the eighties are All-League; ninety and above is the best in the league.

Recalibrated for month two. Everyone in the Sixteen has now played at least 600 minutes across all competitions, so the qualifying line moves from 360 to 600 minutes and the shrinkage constant from 250 to 350. The scale is still set within the season. Movement is shown against the published September 30 grades; a few tenths of it is the recalibration rather than the player.

The holders are not in it

The question from last May, answered

Michigan won the Youth League in May, finished sixth in the Academy, and are not in this season’s competition at all. The five places go to the league’s top five, and there is no automatic entry for the holders. The best side in America on current form is watching the tournament it won.

What it measures

And what it doesn’t

The opponents so far include Olympiacos, Mainz, Rennes, Peñarol and RB Leipzig’s under-19s, and nobody has taken a point off an American club. It is still a group stage. The knockout draw will put Manchester City’s, Bayern’s and Barcelona’s academies in the same bracket, and they are unbeaten too.

The World Cup is twenty-three days away

U.S.A. · 13th in the world · Group F, Qatar

The squad is named, the group is drawn, and two of the three most important Americans are wearing a boot. Christian Pulisic twisted an ankle on October 18 and is due back inside three weeks; Tyler Adams did the same on the 27th and is out for two to four, which puts the opener against Egypt on November 23 right on the edge of his window. The captain, Michael Bradley, is not in the twenty-three at all.

The United States are the second-highest-ranked team in the group and play the lowest-ranked one first. Norway open against Belgium on the same day, at Al-Khor.

How far should they go?

The good version
7 pts

Win the group

Beat Egypt, beat Norway, take a point off the best team in the world with Pulisic back. Top of Group F sends them to the runner-up of Group E — Spain, the Netherlands, South Korea or Paraguay, and most likely one of the first two.

Group: 1stRound of 16Quarter-final
Touchline’s call
4–6 pts

Second, then a wall

Beat Egypt, split Norway, lose to Belgium. Second in the group is the likeliest outcome and it is a good one, but it pairs them with the winner of Group E. We have them out in the round of 16 — having done what a thirteenth-ranked side is supposed to do, and no more.

Group: 2ndRound of 16
The bad version
≤3 pts

Home in December

Drop points to Egypt in the opener without Adams, lose to Norway’s striker, and the Belgium game becomes a formality. It would take two things going wrong, which is exactly what two ankle injuries three weeks out make possible.

Group: 3rd or 4th

The Academy’s share of the squad has fallen from twelve of twenty-three in May to nine, because four of those twelve are now professionals. Counting them, thirteen of the twenty-three have played in this league. The head coach who picks them is the Alabama head coach, whose club visits Michigan on November 12 and who will be in Qatar eleven days later.

Barbados 0, U.S.A. 13

North American U20 Championship · hosted by the U.S.A.

The regional Under-20 championship kicked off on October 27 with thirty-four nations in six first-round groups, and the hosts opened with the biggest scoreline of the tournament: thirteen–nil against Barbados on October 28, in front of 4,348. Cade Cowell scored six — in the 20th, 29th, 47th, 63rd, 70th and 76th minutes. Ricardo Pepi scored three, Brian Gutiérrez three, Danny Leyva one.

The squad. Eighteen of the twenty are Academy players. Texas, Alabama and Michigan supply three each; Ohio State, Georgia and North Carolina two; Miami, Oklahoma and Notre Dame one. Arquimides Ordonez and Gabriel Słonina, both left out in May, are in. The other two are Sean Guadarrama, a sixteen-year-old keeper at West Virginia, and Chicago’s Jack McGlynn.

Still none from USC. The USC head coach picks this squad, and for the third straight tournament he has picked none of his own players. Yunus Musah, fifteen goals and a 76.8 grade for Notre Dame this season, is not in it either.

What’s left. Group F: Cayman Islands on Tuesday, November 1; Guyana on Thursday the 3rd; Honduras, who have won both their games, on Saturday the 5th — all at 17:00. The United States have won this tournament twice running, in 2017 and 2018; Mexico won the three before that.

The Garrett file, No. 3

Rumblings · a recurring item

A date, a stadium, and the other team

For two months this desk has been printing what it could not stand up about a fourteen-year-old from Livonia, Michigan. This month one of those things moved, and it moved a long way. Daniel Garrett will be in Ann Arbor on Saturday, November 12, to watch Michigan play Alabama.

That is the first thing in this file with a date on it. It came to us from two directions that do not usually talk to each other — one at the Michigan end, one that is not — and both gave the same Saturday without being asked for it. We are treating it as solid. We are not treating it as anything more than it is, which is a teenager with a seat at a football match.

But look at the match. It is the evening kick-off, 18:00, on television; Michigan are fourth and Alabama seventh, a point apart. And it is two programmes that will lose wing backs next summer. Michigan’s best, Bret Halsey — 82.4, the third-best inverted wing back in the league — graduates in June. So do two of Alabama’s four, Eddie Munjoma and Charlie Ostrem. Last month we learned that Garrett is an inverted wing back who plays either flank. This month we learned which two clubs he is going to watch doing it.

One more thing about the opponent. The Alabama head coach also picks the United States senior team, and the World Cup starts eleven days after this game. Whether that matters to a fifteen-year-old deciding where to go to school is not something we know. It is a thing a recruiter would mention.

The frame has not changed. We have still not seen him play. The base rate on American fourteen-year-olds who arrive with this kind of noise is poor, and the one everybody remembers from 2004 did not become what he was supposed to. A visit is not an offer, and an offer is not a signature.

Sat12Nov
Michigan v AlabamaUSL Academy · 18:00 · Ann Arbor · televised · 4th v 7th
Seat1visitor

What we can stand up

NameDaniel Garrett
AgeFourteen. Turns fifteen this season.
HomeLivonia, Michigan
NationalityAmerican. Only American.
PositionInverted wing back — either flank
VisitMichigan v Alabama, Ann Arbor, Sat Nov 12
Committed toNobody

What we cannot

  • Whether it is a recruiting visit or a local kid with a ticket. Michigan would not confirm it as either. The Michigan head coach’s office did not respond.
  • Whether Alabama know he will be there — or whether anyone has told them.
  • How good he actually is. Still no club will put a number on him.
  • Which of the Sixteen have watched him. “A few” for three months now, and Michigan is the only name we can attach to anything.
  • Whether there is an offer. From anyone.

The wing-back math, from the save

  • Michigan lose Bret Halsey (82.4, 22) in June; Kevin Paredes (69.1) is nineteen and stays.
  • Alabama lose Eddie Munjoma (65.3) and Charlie Ostrem (50.1); Jacob Greene (65.4) and Erik Dueñas (58.4) stay.
  • Across the league, only three wing backs grade above 80: Booth, López and Halsey. Two of the three graduate next summer.

The Class of 2022, month four

Sixty-seven graduates in their first professional season

The sixty-seven graduates have now made 575 starts between them, up from 301 at the end of September. Mark McKenzie (twenty starts at Columbus) and Tyler Adams (nineteen at Minnesota) have played the most; Christian Pulisic still has the best average rating of any regular, 7.78 from thirteen starts at LAFC, and is now injured with Adams. The best regulars by rating: Christian Pulisic (7.78), Alan Soñora (7.43), Ezequiel Barco (7.39), Auston Trusty (7.35), Matías Succar (7.34).

From the Almanac

Two stories the record office found
Miami

Two Jack Imperatos

Jack Imperato20 · winger · CA 99 / 124
Jack Imperato16 · left back · CA 88 / 134

Miami carry two players with the same name. One is a twenty-year-old winger with 1,076 minutes this season, two goals and six assists; the other is a sixteen-year-old wing back with 1,037 minutes, two goals and one assist. The younger one has the higher ceiling, 134 to 124, and gained four points of ability in October to the elder’s two. The Almanac keeps them apart by their player IDs; the Miami dressing room presumably has its own system.

North Carolina

The only nationality change in the save

Robert Korshunov17 · UNC · CA 103 / 129 · 8 goals this season

Of the 419 players who have appeared in the Academy, exactly one has changed nationality: Robert Korshunov, Russian in May, American by September. He is seventeen, has eight goals and three assists in 1,202 minutes for North Carolina, and is now eligible for the U.S.A. He is not in the Under-20 squad. In a league that supplies eighteen of that squad’s twenty players, he is the one nobody has noticed.

Touchline

Touchline is fiction. It’s an in-universe sports desk for a Football Manager 2022 save. The tables, results, every appearance, goal, assist, rating and ability figure on this page were read from the save on October 31, 2022. Player statistics are all competitions unless a line says league. Head coaches are referred to by role only. Real players appear only through their on-pitch record in the save. Club crests are Touchline’s own designs in each school’s colours, not official marks.

Touchline Grades, the power rankings, the Team of the Month, the 2023 board and the mock draft are this desk’s own models, not figures the game produces. The mock uses today’s USLP table as a stand-in for a draft lottery that has not been run.

Daniel Garrett is a fiction inside a fiction. He does not yet exist in the save, and neither do the people described around him. The Garrett file is a storyline this desk is building in the open, and it will be labelled as such every time it appears until the day he signs somewhere and starts producing numbers like everybody else.

All quotes are invented for this fictional universe. Quotes come only from Touchline’s fictional panel. No real person is quoted.

Season 2, No. 4 · the October edition. Next: the November edition — the World Cup, the Youth League knockout draw, and whatever happens in Ann Arbor.
